m1-ground.title: Ground the data facts: rho source, axis density/mass sensitivity
m1-ground.imperative: Verify the handoff's claim that measured weather (for rho validation) lives in f1_data_<year>.db -- inspect its schema. If Pressure is absent there (as found: only track_temp/air_temp/humidity), trace how session_estimates.rho is actually computed (src/physics/session_fit.py's _density_from_session) to find the REAL measured-pressure source (found: src/data/telemetry_store.py's tele_weather table, pressure_hpa/air_temp_c/humidity_pct, DEFAULT_STORE_PATH=C:/Programs/f1Brainz/data/telemetry_store.db) and confirm it reproduces stored rho bit-for-bit on 2-3 sessions. Inspect estimate_store.py's SYSTEMATIC_FLOOR/_RHO_INFLATION (existing production density/mass-sensitivity grounding for cda/p_max/A0 vs braking/traction) to decide which of the 11 axes get a real density/mass explained component vs an honest physical null. Fit a first-pass within-car-season (fixed-effects) OLS of each axis on ln(rho) to check significance and Mexico/Monaco improvement empirically before committing to the design. Attest c1 with the concrete numbers found.

postconditions.statement: rho source corrected+validated against telemetry_store.db; axis density/mass grouping decided and grounded in estimate_store.py's existing SYSTEMATIC_FLOOR split; empirical beta significance + Mexico/Monaco z-score improvement checked before coding

m2-core.title: layer1_physics.py core: RHO_REF, axis grouping, fit_density_betas, apply_layer1 + unit tests
m2-core.imperative: Create src/physics/weekend_state/layer1_physics.py: RHO_REF derived from ISA constants via moist_air_density_from_pressure (not hardcoded 1.2); DENSITY_SENSITIVE_AXES/MASS_SENSITIVE_AXES grouping grounded in m1's findings; fit_density_betas() (within-car-season fixed-effects OLS of axis on ln(rho), trusted car-seasons >=4 rows); apply_layer1(df) producing per-axis explained/residual/layer1_sigma columns, sigma inflated when rho_is_fallback=1. Write tests/unit/physics/weekend_state/test_layer1_physics.py covering: (a) rho-vs-measured-pressure validation (telemetry_store.db, 2-3 sessions, tight tolerance), (b) sigma inflates on rho_is_fallback=1 (synthetic), (c) explained==0/residual==raw exactly on a density+mass-null axis (honest no-op proof), (d) density beta is statistically significant (|beta|/se large) for drag_area_closed_m2 and max_power_w on real data. Run pytest, iterate to green.

postconditions.statement: layer1_physics.py core + first 4 test cases pass

m3-falsifiable.title: Mexico<->Monaco falsifiable residual-consistency test
m3-falsifiable.imperative: Add mexico_monaco_residual_consistency() helper to layer1_physics.py (per shared-constructor-year raw gap + z, Layer-1-corrected residual gap + z). Add the load-bearing falsifiable test to test_layer1_physics.py: across all shared Mexico/Monaco car-seasons in the real store, assert the Layer-1-corrected mean |z| is meaningfully lower than the raw (density-ignored) mean |z| for drag_area_closed_m2 and max_power_w, with a numeric tolerance such that a mishandled/ignored-density scenario (the raw gap) would fail it. Acknowledge in comments that Mexico differs from Monaco in aero trim/track too (setup confound), so this is a consistency-improvement check, not a claim of exact closure. Run pytest, iterate to green.
